## What to remember {#revision-essentials}

- Embedding lookup yields a vector for each vocabulary ID. A Transformer layer then maintains a hidden state for each sequence position.
- Attention mixes information from accessible positions. In a causal GPT, the current position can use its prefix and its own input.
- The output head uses the final state at a position to score the vocabulary for the next token.

## Recall from memory {#revision-check}

Can two occurrences of “bank” have the same initial embedding and different final states?

<details>
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

Yes. If they have the same ID, their lookup is identical. Different prefixes can lead the layers to produce different final states.

</details>

### A second question to check causality

With parameters and position fixed, can changing a token after the studied position change its hidden state in a causal GPT?

<details>
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. The causal mask prevents that position from accessing the future. A change to the accessible prefix can change its state.

</details>
